purpose: Determine whether catalytic-residue IDENTITY (the active-site nucleophile/base amino acid) can separate the two no-reaction families the reaction representation cannot -- cysteine_protease and ser_his_acid_hydrolase -- which both collapse because they carry NO Rhea reaction.
method: Read-only: for a 22-row sample of each family, fetch the UniProt FASTA by accession and read the amino acid at each annotated ACT_SITE position (1-indexed). No registry mutation; no feature added. Leakage-safe basis (curated active-site residue + sequence = structural/mechanistic evidence, same category as cofactor identity).
verdict: FEASIBLE AND DECISIVE. The catalytic nucleophile identity (Cys vs Ser) is universal within each family and disjoint between them, so a leakage-safe catalytic-residue-identity feature would cleanly separate the families that carry no Rhea reaction. The data is recoverable at zero fetch cost.
implementation_cost: Registry-TOUCHING: requires backfilling the catalytic-residue identity into each bronze row's active_site_residues (FASTA fetch at the annotated positions), then adding catalytic-residue-identity features (cat_res_cys / cat_res_ser / cat_res_his / cat_res_asp_glu / ...) to the leakage-safe representation. The backfill is ADDITIVE (no label/fingerprint/count/benchmark change) but modifies the bronze registry, so it needs explicit authorization per the agent runbook.
leakage_note: Catalytic-residue identity is curated structural/mechanistic evidence (the active-site annotation), NOT EC/name/prose/fingerprint -- the same leakage-safe category as cofactor identity and the existing residue-role ratios.
